NATIONAL COMPANY LAW APPELLATE TRIBUNAL,
PRINCIPAL BENCH, NEW DELHI

Company Appeal (AT) (Insolvency) No. 1940 of 2026

In the matter of:

Bharat Ajay Jaisinghani Suspended Director of Polycab
India Limited
....Appellant
Vs.

Asier Metals Pvt. Ltd. & Anr.
...Respondents
For Appellant
Mr. Arun Kathpalia, Sr. Advocate with Mr. Suhail
Nathani, Mr. Anuj Tiwari, Mr. Dinesh Pednekar,
Mr.
Chanakya
Keswani,
Ms.
Shubhangi
Khandelwal, Ms. Prapti Allagh, Ms. Diksha Gupta,
Mr. Shivendra Nath Mishra, Mr. Vaibhav Vats, Mr.
Sameer Mishra, Advocates.
For Respondents
Mr. Krishnendu Datta, Mr. Anand Chhibbar, Sr.
Advocates with Mr. Mohit Chaudhary, Mr. Kanishk
Khetan, Advocates for R1
Mr. Sunil Shah, IRP.
ORDER
(Hybrid Mode)

09.10.2026:
This Appeal is filed against an impugned order dated
07.10.2026 passed by the Ld. Adjudicating Authority (National Company Law
Tribunal)
Division
Bench,
Court-I,
Ahmedabad
in
CP
(IB)
No.273/9/AHM/2026. It is submitted by the Ld. Senior Counsel for the
Appellant at the outset, without prejudice to the rights and contentions, the
Appellant is inclined to deposit the entire amount as stated in Part IV of the
application under Section 9 IBC. Further, it is submitted by the Ld. Senior
Counsel for the Appellant there exist a pre-existing dispute between the parties
qua the payments made and the credit notes to be issued by the Operational
Creditor which dispute has since been recorded in the correspondence

2

Company Appeal (AT) (Insolvency) No. 1940 of 2026
between the parties but instead of issuing the credit notes, a notice under
Section 8 was issued on 06.08.2026 by the Respondent and shortly thereafter,
on 24.08.2026, a petition under Section 9 IBC was filed and the impugned
order was thus passed on 07.10.2026. Learned Senior Counsel for the
Appellant has also referred to the status of the Appellant as mentioned in
paragraphs 7.2 and 7.3 of this Appeal as under:-
“7.2.
Polycab
is
India’s
largest
integrated
manufacturer of wires and cables. It also carries on an
FMCG business and undertakes turnkey EHV, MV and
LV cabling and power projects. It operates 27
manufacturing plants across Gujarat, Maharashtra,
Karnataka, Uttarakhand, Tamil Nadu and Daman, 3
regional offices, 35 warehouses and depots, 12 branch
offices and 14 experience centres, and has over 3,900
dealers and distributors and over 1,90,000 retail
outlets. As on 31.03.2026, Polycab employed 4,574
persons directly and 13,642 persons indirectly.
7.3. Polycab’s standalone revenue for the financial
year 2025-26 was INR 2,81,851.77 million, and its
aggregate revenue for the last five financial years is
INR 9,41,594.58 million. In the same period, it paid
direct taxes aggregating INR 26,993.73 million and
declared dividends aggregating INR 16,361.95 million.
Polycab’s shares are listed on the BSE and the NSE;
as on 31.03.2026 it had 3,62,997 shareholders and a
market capitalisation of INR 1,030.29 billion. Polycab
has availed working capital limits of INR 12,000 crore
from a consortium of 10 banks, which hold a charge
over its assets. A true copy of the Annual Report of

3

Company Appeal (AT) (Insolvency) No. 1940 of 2026
Polycab for the financial year ended 31.03.2026 is
annexed as Annexure A-3.”
2.
Though the existence of dispute has been agitated by the Ld. Senior
Counsel for the Respondent but suffice is to say that considering the status of
the Appellant as above as also the fact the Appellant is inclined to deposit an
amount as stated in Part-IV of the petition, though without prejudice to its
rights and contentions, let the said amount be deposited by way of FDR, in
the name of ‘Registrar, National Company Law Appellate Tribunal, New Delhi’
within a week from today and that the impugned order is stayed and be kept
in abeyance till further orders.
3.
List the Appeal on 26.10.2026 within 1st five cases.

[Justice Yogesh Khanna]
Officiating Chairperson

[Barun Mitra]
Member (Technical)

(Ajai Das Mehrotra)
Member (Technical)
Anjali/md
